prompts.prompt:
Bowdoin believes that its broadly diverse and inclusive campus community prepares graduates to be contributing and useful citizens of the world. Every graduate of this institution should be confident in their preparation to be able to navigate through differences and in all sorts of situations. A Bowdoin education does not guarantee these skills, but it does impart a set of tools necessary to bravely enter unfamiliar conditions with the confidence to deal effectively with ambiguity.
If you wish, you may share anything about the unique experiences and perspectives that you would bring with you to the Bowdoin campus and community or an experience you have had that required you to navigate across or through difference.

sources.title: Bowdoin Admissions: Apply (Bowdoin Supplement, optional essays)
Bowdoin Student Aid: International Students (Class of 2031)

notes: Both essays are optional (max 250 words each) and sit in the Bowdoin Supplement: the 'Questions' section of the Common App, or a separate web form for Coalition on Scoir and QuestBridge applicants. The supplement also has non-essay questions (such as the test-optional choice and how you learned about Bowdoin) that the page does not itemize. The prompts are not labelled with a cycle year; the cycle is inferred from the same page referencing the 2027-2028 CSS Profile and the aid page naming the Class of 2031. No proof-of-funds / I-20 financial document requirement is published on the admissions, student aid or incoming-international-student pages read, so intl_finance is null. What is published: international applicants (not Canadians) submit aid materials (CSS Profile, parents' 2025 tax or income documents via IDOC) only after admission, within seven days of the offer, and Bowdoin issues the I-20 after admission. Ask the Student Aid Office (sao@bowdoin.edu) or Admissions what funding proof the I-20 needs.
